guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints figures revealed - Q1 2024
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly provider complaint patterns are aggregate service-quality evidence and cannot verify broadband availability, orderability or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q1 2024 complaints update on 25 July 2024.
The figures cover January to March 2024.
Overall complaints fell compared with the previous quarter.
Landline, fixed-broadband and pay-TV complaints fell.
Mobile-service complaints increased slightly.
NOW Broadband generated the most broadband complaints.
Sky and Shell Energy generated the fewest broadband complaints.
NOW Broadband, EE and Virgin Media were the most complained-about landline providers.
Utility Warehouse generated the fewest landline complaints.
O2 remained the most complained-about mobile operator.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q2 2024 complaints update on 14 November 2024.
The figures cover April to June 2024.
Overall complaints remained at a similar level to the previous quarter.
Broadband, landline and mobile complaints fell slightly.
Pay-TV complaints stayed the same.
NOW Broadband generated the most broadband complaints.
Sky generated the fewest broadband complaints.
EE generated the most landline complaints.
O2 generated the most mobile complaints.
EE and Virgin Media generated the most pay-TV complaints.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q3 2024 complaints update on 13 February 2025.
The figures cover July to September 2024.
There was a slight decrease in complaints from the previous quarter.
The overall industry complaint level stayed broadly the same.
TalkTalk generated the most broadband complaints.
Sky generated the fewest broadband complaints.
EE, NOW Broadband and TalkTalk were the most complained-about landline providers.
Utility Warehouse generated the fewest landline complaints.
O2 remained the most complained-about mobile provider.
EE and Virgin Media were the most complained-about pay-TV providers.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q4 2024 complaints update on 1 May 2025.
The figures cover October to December 2024.
Overall complaint numbers remained similar to the previous quarter.
Broadband, mobile and pay-TV complaints decreased slightly.
Landline complaints stayed the same.
NOW Broadband and TalkTalk generated the most broadband complaints.

NOW Broadband generated the most landline complaints.

EE and Virgin Media generated the most pay-TV complaints.

guard_streams.write_limit: National and postcode-level coverage statistics are dated aggregate evidence; selected-parcel serviceability requires exact current premises data and orderability validation.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Spring 2024 update on 24 April 2024.
The report is based on fixed and mobile coverage as of January 2024.
Gigabit-capable broadband reached 24.0 million homes, or 80%.
Full-fibre coverage reached 18.7 million homes, or 62%.
UK superfast coverage remained at 97%.
Around 57,000 premises could not access decent broadband.
Around 47,000 of those premises were not expected to be covered by public rollout within twelve months.
Around 93% of UK landmass had predicted good outdoor 4G from at least one operator.
Around 92% of premises could receive an outdoor 5G signal from at least one operator at high confidence.
Ofcom published postcode, output-area, constituency, authority and UK/nations data downloads.
